title: Globular Cluster Messier 4 (M4)
caption: Globular cluster Messier 4, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: M 4, Messier 4, NGC 6121 · constellation Scorpius · about 7,000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Thousands of points of light fill a black field, growing somewhat more crowded toward the center. The most prominent stars look blue or yellow-orange, and the brightest carry four diffraction spikes. This is Messier 4, the closest globular star cluster to Earth, a dense collection of several hundred thousand stars in the constellation Scorpius. NASA has given its distance as both 6,000 and 7,000 light-years.

Astronomers suspect an unseen black hole sits at its core, with a mass of as much as 800 times that of our Sun. That would make it an intermediate-mass black hole, a rare missing link between the small black holes left by exploded stars and the supermassive ones at the centers of galaxies.

Eduardo Vitral of the Space Telescope Science Institute and his team worked out the object's mass from the motions of stars around it, using 12 years of Hubble observations. They found a lot of mass packed into a very tiny region, which Vitral says is hard to explain as anything other than a single black hole.

understand.summary: Taken with the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. F435W is shown in blue, F606W in green and F814W in red.
understand.eye: The F814W filter reaches into near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and the colors are assigned to three separate filter images.

explore: The alternative would need roughly 40 smaller black holes, by the team's estimate, squeezed into a region just one-tenth of a light-year wide, and such a crowd would be unstable, merging or flinging members out. Vitral cautions that a stellar mechanism unknown to current physics cannot be ruled out. Other suspected intermediate-mass black holes, such as one in Omega Centauri, remain inconclusive.
sources: NASA release: NASA’s Hubble Hunts for Intermediate-Sized Black Hole Close to Home
